newsitem.title: UK: Plane comes off runway at London airport.
newsitem.headline: Plane comes off runway at London airport.

text.p: More than 40 passengers were evacuated from a Dutch passenger plane on Sunday after its undercarriage collapsed on landing at London's Heathrow Airport, eyewitnesses said.
The KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV Fokker 50 plane had 41 passengers and four crew on board when it belly-flopped and then veered 50 yards (metres) off the runway, they said.
There were no reports of injuries.
A spokeswoman for Heathrow Airport said the plane had come down on the southern runway which was still closed.
"This means that all take-offs and landings are on the northern runway which is obviously causing some delays to flights," she said.
An eyewitness said he believed the pilot plane had saved the lives of passengers.
Airport security guard Kailash Joshi said: "It was very dramatic -- my legs are still shaking even now.
"I give full credit to the pilot for landing as well as he did considering the circumstances. He definitely saved some lives. I think everyone watching was expecting the worst."
